record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: If a homology sphere S occurs as the boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2, must S be diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere S^3?

evidence.quote:
QUESTION. Let a homology sphere S be a boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex
domain in C2
. Is it true that then S is diffeomorphic to S
3
?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ be a relatively compact domain with smooth boundary $S = \partial\Omega$, and assume that $\Omega$ is strictly pseudoconvex, meaning that there exists a smooth defining function $\rho$ for $\Omega$ (with $\Omega = \{\rho < 0\}$ and $d\rho \neq 0$ on $S$) whose complex Hessian $\big(\partial^2\rho/\partial z_i\partial\bar z_j\big)$ is positive definite on the complex tangent space at every point of $S$. Suppose further that $S$ is a (closed, oriented) integral homology 3-sphere, i.e., $H_*(S;\mathbb{Z}) \cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb{Z})$. Must $S$ be diffeomorphic to the standard 3-sphere $S^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a definitive resolution. Related work studies strictly pseudoconvex 3-manifolds bounding domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ (e.g., Kruzhilin on 2-spheres in such boundaries, and recent work on obstruction-flat boundaries), but no source clearly settles whether every homology 3-sphere bounding a strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3$.

status_evidence.title: Two-dimensional spheres in the boundaries of strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^2 (Kruzhilin)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical work on spheres in boundaries of strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^2.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on the topology of boundaries of strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^2, but does not settle the homology sphere question.

status_evidence.title: Bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^2 with obstruction flat boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Concerns strictly pseudoconvex domains in C^2 diffeomorphic to the ball.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research considers strictly pseudoconvex boundaries diffeomorphic to S^3, indicating the topological classification of such boundaries remains a live topic.
